span.p: No — I am dividing profit by REVENUE

span.p: I need to apply a profit percentage to a bid or change order

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Am I dividing profit by COST?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
That is MARKUP
Markup % = Profit ÷ Direct Cost
Example: $20 profit on $100 cost = 20% markup → $120 bid price

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
That is MARGIN
Margin % = Profit ÷ Revenue
Example: $20 profit on $120 revenue = 16.7% margin

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Is my TARGET stated as markup or margin?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Apply the markup %: Bid Price = Cost × (1 + Markup%)
Example: 20% markup → Cost × 1.20

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Convert to markup first: Markup% = Margin% ÷ (1 - Margin%)
Example: 20% margin → 20% ÷ 80% = 25% markup → Cost × 1.25

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Did I state the basis in the estimate or CO?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
GO BACK — always state 'X% markup on cost' or 'Y% gross margin on revenue'
Confusing them on a $5M job = $165K error at 20% target

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
